newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo lifts profits on back of associates.
newsitem.headline: Anglo lifts profits on back of associates.

text.p: True to expectations, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's associate companies helped swell its headline earnings per share by 23 percent when the group announced year results on Tuesday.

"The associates' contribution of 7,597 million rand to net income before taxation rose by 25 percent, largely as a result of much improved operating results from diamonds, gold and mining finance interests," Anglo said in a statement.

South Africa's biggest company posted headline EPS of 2,144 cents, within the range predicted by analysts although a little below the consensus of 2,220.5. However, the dividend was a little higher than the expected 690 cents at 700.

Anglo's net income before tax for the year ended March 31 rose to 11,098 million rand from 7,761 million rand previously. "1996/97 was a pleasing year, with significantly improved headline earnings, further expansion of our operations, and more recently, the completion of major black empowerment initiatives," Anglo chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said.
Analysts said rich profits from sister companies diamond giant De Beers Consolidated and offshore mining financial company Minorco SA had contributed to Anglo's earnings.

Anglo said investment earnings from diamond interests contributed 17 percent to the total (against 16 percent in 1996), industry and commerce contributed 34 percent (39 percent), gold contributed 15 percent (nine percent), coal contributed eight percent (eight percent), financial services and property 14 percent (19 percent) and platinum, base metals and other mining 12 percent (nine percent).

Dividend income from general investments increased 20 percent to 365 million rand, largely because of increased distributions from diamond trading companies and the first dividend from Lonrho, Anglo said.
Trading income grew 36 percent to 1,040 million rand, reflecting buoyant market conditions enjoyed by its subsidiary Anglo American Coal Corp Ltd (Amcoal).
The surplus on realisation of investments of 2,116 million rand from 485 million rand arose mainly from the sale of a 35 percent interest in Johnnic to the National Empowerment Consortium.
"The balance of the surplus was obtained from a number of transactions including the sale of certain non-strategic gold and industrial holdings and an exchange of mineral rights."

Anglo said it considered it prudent to augment the level of provisions by setting aside 288 million rand to cover mainly the decline in market values of its investments in Del Monte Royal Foods and Lonrho Plc.
Prospecting costs increased by 28 percent to 190 million rand as a result of increased exploration activity in sub-Saharan west and east Africa.
